stem: A retail company's ADK support agent forgets user preferences between conversations. They want long-term, per-user personalization with the least custom code and no self-managed database. What should the architect use?

options.A: Store each conversation in Firestore and load the full history into the prompt on every turn
options.B: Use Agent Platform Sessions to persist events and Memory Bank to generate per-user memories from them
options.C: Keep ADK's in-memory session service and increase the model's context window
options.D: Cache the last N turns in Memorystore for Redis keyed by user ID

rationale.A: Custom code, and puts the whole history in every prompt; no distilled long-term memories
rationale.B: Sessions record chronological events; Memory Bank's GenerateMemories extracts per-user facts scoped by user ID for future sessions — the managed answer
rationale.C: In-memory sessions vanish on restart and a larger context is not cross-session memory
rationale.D: Redis is short-term state, not generated long-term memory, and is self-designed

stem: A team wants to try Agent Platform Sessions from their local ADK app before deploying anything. What is the minimum they must do?

options.A: Deploy the agent to Agent Runtime first; Sessions are only available to deployed agents
options.B: Create an Agent Runtime instance (no code deployed) and point ADK's VertexAiSessionService at it
options.C: Enable Firestore and write a custom BaseSessionService
options.D: Deploy to Cloud Run with the ADK template; Sessions are provisioned automatically

rationale.A: The docs state you do not need to deploy code to use Sessions
rationale.B: An Agent Runtime instance created without a deployment acts as the session store; ADK's VertexAiSessionService uses its ID
rationale.C: Possible but not the managed path asked for
rationale.D: Cloud Run deployment does not provision Sessions

stem: A bank must run an agent that classifies internal documents containing PII. Data cannot leave their VPC, latency must be low, and the task is narrow. Which model strategy best fits?

options.A: Gemini via the SaaS API with a data-processing addendum
options.B: A self-hosted open-weights small language model from Model Garden deployed on GKE inside the VPC
options.C: The largest proprietary LLM available, for maximum accuracy
options.D: A self-hosted large open-weights model on a single GPU node

rationale.A: May meet compliance in general, but the stated constraint is data never leaves the VPC
rationale.B: Narrow task + residency + latency points to a small self-hosted model; Model Garden provides open weights
rationale.C: Size is not the requirement; residency and latency are
rationale.D: A large model raises cost and latency for a narrow task

stem: A developer wants to iterate on an ADK agent's tools and prompts with a chat UI before any cloud deployment. What is the intended workflow?

options.A: Deploy to Agent Runtime after every change and test through the console
options.B: Run the ADK local dev server (adk web) and interact on localhost
options.D: Write unit tests only; ADK has no local interactive mode

rationale.A: Slow and billable; not needed for local iteration
rationale.B: ADK ships a local web UI; the Memory Bank quickstart itself tests against the localhost server
rationale.C: CX Agent Studio is the low-code product, not an ADK runner
rationale.D: ADK has a local interactive runner

stem: An enterprise wants its coding assistants and developers to scaffold, evaluate, and deploy ADK agents with consistent, reusable skills and a project manifest. Which tool provides this?

options.B: Agents CLI in Agent Platform
options.D: Skill Registry read through the console

rationale.A: Antigravity loads skills, but the scaffolding/eval/deploy skills and manifest come from Agents CLI
rationale.B: Agents CLI scaffolds a project (agents-cli-manifest.yaml) and installs specialized skills for scaffolding, evaluation and deployment
rationale.C: A catalog of agents and tools; it does not scaffold projects
rationale.D: Skill Registry stores skills; Agents CLI is how a workflow uses them

stem: Twelve agents in a project share one service account. Auditors cannot tell which agent accessed which resource, and the account has accumulated broad roles. What is the recommended fix?

options.A: Create one service account per agent and rotate keys monthly
options.B: Assign each agent an Agent Identity and grant least-privilege roles to that principal
options.C: Put all agents behind a single Cloud Run service with IAP
options.D: Log tool calls to BigQuery and analyse them

rationale.A: Still key management, and lacks agent-specific attestation and audit fields
rationale.B: Agent Identity gives a unique attested identity (SPIFFE ID) per agent, replaces shared service accounts, and audit logs show agent and user
rationale.C: IAP protects the endpoint; it does not separate agent principals

stem: An agent with an Agent Identity must read objects from a Cloud Storage bucket. Granting roles/storage.legacyBucketReader fails. What should you do?

options.A: Grant the legacy role at the project level instead
options.B: Grant a standard role such as roles/storage.objectViewer to the agent identity
options.C: Switch the agent to a service account key

rationale.A: Legacy bucket roles cannot be granted to agent identities at any level
rationale.B: The documented limitation is only for legacy bucket roles; standard IAM storage roles work
rationale.C: Reverts to the anti-pattern Agent Identity replaces

stem: A partner's agent runs outside Google Cloud but must be discoverable and governed alongside your agents. How do you bring it into Agent Registry?

options.A: Redeploy it to Agent Runtime; that is the only supported way
options.B: Use Agent Registry's manual registration for externally hosted agents
options.C: Register its endpoint in Agent Gateway; the registry is populated automatically
options.D: Add it as an MCP server in Antigravity

rationale.A: Automatic registration is for supported runtimes; external hosting has its own path
rationale.B: The docs send externally hosted or unsupported-runtime agents to manual registration
rationale.C: Gateway looks up the registry; it does not populate it

stem: You deploy an A2A-compliant agent to Agent Runtime. What happens with Agent Registry?

options.A: Nothing until you call the Agent Registry API
options.B: Registration is automatic and the agent's A2A skills are extracted from its metadata
options.C: You must add an opt-in flag on every subsequent update
options.D: Only the Gemini Enterprise runtime registers automatically

rationale.A: Manual API calls are for unsupported runtimes
rationale.B: Agent Runtime deployments register automatically; A2A skills are read from the agent's metadata
rationale.C: Opt-in configuration applies to some other runtimes, not Agent Runtime
rationale.D: Agent Runtime is documented as automatic

stem: A RAG agent returns relevant documents in the top 50 but the top 3 used in the prompt are often off-topic. What is the most targeted improvement?

options.A: Increase the number of chunks passed to the model to 50
options.B: Add a reranking step over the vector-similarity candidates before selecting the top 3
options.C: Switch to a larger embedding model

rationale.A: Blows up context cost and does not fix ordering
rationale.B: Recall is fine; precision at the top is the problem, which is what a reranker addresses
rationale.C: May help recall; the stated problem is ordering among already-retrieved candidates

stem: Two teams built agents on different frameworks; a planning agent must delegate subtasks to the other agent and receive results. Which protocol is designed for this?

options.A: MCP, because it standardises tool calling
options.B: A2A, which lets agents declare capabilities and exchange tasks

rationale.A: MCP connects an agent to tools and servers; agent-to-agent delegation is A2A's role
rationale.B: A2A is the open standard for agents declaring identity/capabilities and interoperating
rationale.D: Works, but the exam asks for the agentic protocol

stem: A workflow needs three independent lookups (inventory, pricing, shipping) and then a summary. Latency matters. Which ADK composition fits?

options.A: A single LLM agent that calls the three tools one after another
options.B: A ParallelAgent for the three lookups followed by a sequential summary step
options.C: A SequentialAgent for all four steps
options.D: Three separate deployments coordinated by Cloud Scheduler

rationale.A: Serialises independent work through one reasoning loop
rationale.B: Independent subtasks fan out in parallel; the dependent summary runs after
rationale.C: Adds latency with no benefit for independent steps
rationale.D: Scheduler is time-based, not request-time orchestration

stem: An Agent Runtime agent behind Agent Gateway must call a tool hosted in a different project. What is required?

options.A: Nothing; cross-project calls are allowed by default
options.B: Register the destination in the Agent Registry of the gateway's project, using Agent-to-Anywhere mode
options.C: Move the tool into the gateway's project

rationale.A: Every destination must be registered and authorised
rationale.B: The setup guide: cross-project destinations must be registered in the gateway project and are only valid for Runtime agents in Agent-to-Anywhere (egress) mode
rationale.D: Client-to-Agent is ingress, not agent-to-tool egress

stem: You want to check, on every pull request, that an ADK agent still calls the right tools in the right order for 40 known scenarios. Which tooling fits?

options.A: Manual chat testing in adk web
options.B: An ADK evalset with expected tool trajectories, run in CI

rationale.B: ADK evaluation tooling compares tool trajectories and responses against a saved evalset

stem: Product managers want production answers scored for helpfulness and groundedness against a rubric, at scale, without writing a scorer. What should you use?

options.B: Agent Platform Gen AI evaluation service with rubric-based metrics

rationale.A: Valid when metrics are bespoke; the requirement is to avoid writing a scorer
rationale.B: The managed evaluation service provides model-based metrics; the Runtime docs list it under quality and evaluation
rationale.C: Checks tool order, not answer quality

stem: Which addition most improves a golden test set that currently contains only typical, well-formed user requests?

options.A: More examples of the same typical requests
options.B: Edge cases: ambiguous, out-of-scope, adversarial and multi-step requests with expected behaviour
options.C: Only prompts the model already answers correctly

rationale.B: The guide names golden data, prompts and edge cases as the parts of an agent test set
rationale.D: Unlabeled data is not golden data

stem: A RAG agent's answers degraded after a document refresh, but tool calls are unchanged. Which evaluation would detect this in the future?

options.B: A golden-dataset evaluation that scores retrieval quality alongside response quality
options.D: Unit tests of the embedding function

rationale.A: Trajectories were unchanged; the failure is in what was retrieved
rationale.B: The guide asks for evaluating both response and retrieval quality against a golden dataset
rationale.D: Function tests pass; the corpus changed

stem: A startup with no platform team needs to ship an ADK agent with managed sessions, memory and built-in observability, with the least operational work. Which runtime?

options.A: GKE with a custom Helm chart
options.B: Agent Runtime
options.C: Cloud Run with Firestore for sessions
options.D: Compute Engine VMs behind a load balancer

rationale.B: Agent Runtime is the fully managed runtime with Sessions, Memory Bank and observability integrated
rationale.C: Serverless, but sessions and memory become your code

stem: An agent needs a custom sidecar, a GPU-backed local model and node-level network policies. Which runtime should the architect choose?

options.B: GKE

rationale.A: A managed runtime does not expose sidecars or node configuration
rationale.B: Kubernetes gives sidecars, GPU node pools and network policies
rationale.C: Supports sidecars and some GPU configurations, but not node-level network policy
rationale.D: A workspace product, not a runtime for custom containers

stem: An Agent Runtime agent's tool calls fail with 403 'Egress request is not authorized'. What is the first thing to check?

options.B: The IAM roles bound to the agent identity principal and the Gateway authorization policy, using the ReasoningEngine logs to find the failing calls

rationale.B: The troubleshooting guide: confirm it is a Gateway egress error, query logs with resource.type aiplatform.googleapis.com/ReasoningEngine, verify the roles on the agent identity principal
rationale.C: Agent Runtime is not Cloud Run

stem: An agent occasionally repeats the same tool call dozens of times before timing out. What is the best combination of fixes?

options.B: Cap iterations / add loop detection in the orchestration, and use Cloud Trace to see the repeated spans and the state that triggers them

rationale.B: Reasoning loops need a termination guard plus traces to find the trigger; the guide lists loops as a troubleshooting topic and Cloud Trace as the tool
rationale.C: May change behaviour but does not prevent loops
rationale.D: Removes the capability instead of the fault

stem: End-to-end response time rose from 2 s to 9 s after adding two tools. How do you find which step is responsible?

options.A: Read Cloud Logging text lines and estimate
options.B: Use Cloud Trace spans per tool invocation to compare durations
options.D: Ask the model to explain its latency

rationale.B: Google Cloud Observability (Cloud Trace) is the in-scope tool for latency bottlenecks

stem: Security wants to guarantee an agent can never reach resources outside a defined set, regardless of roles granted later by mistake. Which mechanism?

options.A: Organization policy constraints on the project
options.B: A principal access boundary (PAB) policy attached via Agent Identity

rationale.A: Constrains resource configuration, not what a principal can access
rationale.B: PAB policies bound the set of resources a principal may access; the guide names PAB via Agent Identity

stem: You are introducing Agent Gateway and worry a mis-scoped policy will break production agents on day one. What does Google recommend?

options.A: Skip the authorization policy; it is optional
options.B: Deploy IAP in dry-run mode first to validate the policy without blocking traffic
options.D: Route only Gemini Enterprise agents through the gateway

rationale.A: Every Agent Gateway requires an authorization policy
rationale.B: The setup guide recommends IAP dry-run mode initially to validate without blocking
rationale.D: Managed runtimes route through the gateway automatically anyway

stem: Prompts reaching your agents through the gateway must be screened for prompt injection, jailbreaks and sensitive-data leakage. Which integration?

options.B: Model Armor templates delegated from Agent Gateway

rationale.B: Agent Gateway delegates AI content sanitisation to Model Armor templates with the required safety filters
rationale.C: A catalog, not a content filter
rationale.D: An HTTP WAF, not an LLM content guard

stem: An agent acts on behalf of end users against a SaaS API with their delegated credentials. Compliance requires the agent code never sees raw credentials. Which design meets this?

options.A: Pass the user's token in the prompt
options.B: Agent Identity with Agent Gateway: the auth manager encrypts end-user credentials and the gateway decrypts them at egress
options.C: Store credentials in the session state
options.D: Use a single service account for all users

rationale.A: Exposes the credential to the model and logs
rationale.B: The Agent Identity docs describe exactly this: credentials encrypted by the auth manager, decrypted at the gateway, never available to the agent
rationale.C: Session state is readable by agent code

stem: An agent can issue customer refunds. Finance requires refunds above a threshold be approved by a person, with an audit trail. What should the architect add?

options.A: A stricter system prompt telling the model to be careful
options.B: A human-in-the-loop approval step for the high-value tool call, with the decision logged

rationale.B: HITL is the guardrail the guide lists for consequential actions; it gives control and auditability
rationale.C: Capability is not the issue; authority is

stem: After an incident, auditors ask which agent and which user triggered a specific database read. Which design makes this answerable from logs?

options.A: Shared service account with request IDs
options.B: Per-agent Agent Identity acting on behalf of the user, so audit logs carry both identities

rationale.A: Shared accounts erase the agent principal
rationale.B: Agent Identity's observability benefit: when acting on a user's behalf, logs show both identities

stem: Developers want a coding agent to query the company's internal issue tracker and read design docs while coding, without pasting them into prompts. What should you configure?

options.B: MCP servers for the tracker and docs in the coding agent's configuration (Antigravity or Claude Code)
options.C: A cron job that emails the docs

rationale.A: Does not give the agent access
rationale.B: MCP is how coding agents get tool access; the guide names MCP servers, skills and tools in Antigravity and Claude Code on Google Cloud
rationale.D: Data plumbing without an agent interface

stem: A coding agent must run and test untrusted third-party code from pull requests. Which environment is appropriate?

options.B: An isolated sandbox such as a GKE workload or Cloud Workstations with restricted egress
options.C: The production cluster with a separate namespace
options.D: A shared CI runner with cached credentials

rationale.A: Untrusted code on a machine with credentials
rationale.B: The guide lists GKE, Cloud Workstations and Antigravity sandboxes for running coding agents securely
rationale.D: Cached credentials plus untrusted code is the classic exfiltration path

stem: A coding agent proposes a patch for an application-layer vulnerability. What should the workflow require before merge?

options.A: Trust the agent; it explained the fix
options.B: Regression tests plus a re-run of the security scanner on the patched code, reviewed by a human

rationale.B: Agent-authored security fixes need the same evidence as human ones: tests, scanner, review
rationale.D: Formatting says nothing about the vulnerability

stem: A team migrating from Gemini CLI asks which Google tool is its successor for terminal-based agentic coding.

options.B: Antigravity CLI

rationale.A: Agents CLI targets Agent Platform workflows (scaffold/eval/deploy), not the Gemini CLI role
rationale.B: Third-party integration docs describe Antigravity CLI as Gemini CLI's direct successor; verify against official Antigravity docs
rationale.C: gcloud is the cloud CLI, not a coding agent
rationale.D: An editor, not an agent CLI

stem: Every engineer should get the same house-style instructions and workflow steps in Antigravity for any project they open. Where should these live?

options.B: As skills in the global Antigravity skills directory (or a shared repo cloned there)
options.D: In the model's system prompt via API

rationale.B: Antigravity loads SKILL.md directories; project scope under .agent/skills, global scope under the user's Antigravity skills folder
rationale.D: Antigravity is not configured that way

stem: You want a check to run automatically every time the coding agent is about to execute a shell command, blocking dangerous ones. Which customisation type is this?

options.B: A hook

rationale.A: Instructions/resources the agent loads for a task
rationale.B: Hooks run at lifecycle events such as before a tool executes

stem: After building an agent with Antigravity, the team wants to deploy, govern and monitor it on Agent Platform from the same workflow. What augments Antigravity for this?

options.B: Cloud Build only

rationale.A: The guide: augment Antigravity with Agents CLI to build, scale, govern and optimize deployed agents
rationale.B: Builds artifacts; not the agent-platform workflow
rationale.C: Low-code authoring, not deployment of code agents

stem: A customer-service flow must collect an order number, then a reason, then confirm — in that order, with deterministic branching and no code. Which tool and construct?

options.B: CX Agent Studio with pages, transition routes and event handlers
options.C: Gemini Enterprise Agent Designer free-form instructions

rationale.B: The guide names state-based workflows (pages, transition routes, event handlers) in CX Agent Studio
rationale.C: Instruction-driven; deterministic multi-page state machines are CX Agent Studio's model

stem: A low-code agent answers correctly but in inconsistent formats. Without code, what is the most direct fix?

options.B: Add few-shot examples of the desired format to the in-console prompt template / system instructions

rationale.A: Format consistency is a prompting problem first
rationale.B: The guide lists few-shot and chain-of-thought prompt templates in Agent Designer / CX Agent Studio

stem: In a CX Agent Studio flow, the user says something the current page cannot match. Which construct should handle it gracefully?

options.A: A transition route to the same page
options.B: An event handler (no-match / no-input) on the page or flow
options.C: A webhook that restarts the session

rationale.B: Event handlers exist for events like no-match and no-input

stem: Employees should ask a Gemini Enterprise agent questions over internal wikis and drives while seeing only documents they already have access to. What should the architect configure?

options.A: Export all documents to a public bucket and index them
options.B: Connect the sources via Gemini Enterprise data connectors / Agent Search with source ACLs enforced
options.C: Copy documents into the system prompt
options.D: Give the agent an owner-level service account

rationale.B: The guide names Gemini Enterprise and Agent Search for securely connecting and querying proprietary data
rationale.C: Does not scale and leaks across users

stem: A media company wants agents to answer questions about the content of thousands of training videos and call recordings. What must the pipeline do first?

options.A: Store the files in Cloud SQL
options.B: Ingest and process the unstructured multimodal data (video, audio) so it becomes searchable and groundable in the workflow
options.C: Ask the model to watch the videos on demand at query time

rationale.A: Relational storage does not make media searchable
rationale.B: The guide lists ingesting and processing unstructured multimodal data as a 1.2 skill

stem: A multi-agent system makes hundreds of small routing decisions per user request and one complex planning step. Costs are too high. What should the architect change first?

options.A: Use the largest model everywhere for consistency
options.B: Use a small language model for routing/classification and reserve the LLM for the planning step
options.D: Move everything to a self-hosted GPU cluster

rationale.B: Match model size to step complexity; the guide's LLM-vs-SLM axis
rationale.D: Changes hosting, not the per-call waste

stem: A company wants to compare several open-weight models before choosing one for self-hosting on GKE. Where on Google Cloud does it discover and try them?

options.B: Model Garden

rationale.B: Model Garden: 200+ models from Google, partners and OSS for discovery and experimentation

stem: Which pairing is the most defensible when the dominant constraint is 'no ML operations team and the product must ship in two weeks'?

options.B: Gemini via the managed API

rationale.B: Managed SaaS removes serving, scaling and patching work

stem: A regulator requires model weights and prompts to stay inside a specific region and be auditable. Which axis of the guide's model-selection criteria dominates?

options.B: Security and data residency

rationale.B: Residency/audit is a security constraint and decides hosting model first

stem: An agent must summarise 200-page contracts with high accuracy and no strict latency target. What is the reasonable choice?

options.B: A large, long-context proprietary or open LLM

rationale.A: Quality and context length dominate here
rationale.B: Long context + reasoning quality matters more than speed

stem: Which statement about open-source vs proprietary models is the exam-safe one?

options.A: Open-source is always cheaper end to end
options.B: Proprietary SaaS trades control and residency for lower operational burden; open weights trade the reverse
options.C: Proprietary models cannot be used on Google Cloud
options.D: Open weights cannot run on GKE

rationale.A: Serving costs and ops can exceed API costs
rationale.B: The trade-off framing the guide's axes imply

stem: In ADK terms, what turns a user message into a stream of function-call and function-response events for an agent?

options.B: The Runner, using a session service

rationale.A: Defines instruction and tools; does not execute turns
rationale.B: The Runner drives execution and yields events

stem: A team wants to package an ADK agent into a container image and run it locally with the dev UI before choosing a cloud runtime. Which command?

options.B: adk deploy docker --with_ui <agent-folder>

rationale.B: Builds a Docker image with the UI included

stem: Which is true about ADK?

options.A: It only works with Gemini models
options.B: It is an open-source, code-first, model-agnostic toolkit for building, evaluating and deploying agents
options.C: It is the low-code canvas in Gemini Enterprise
options.D: It requires Agent Runtime to run

rationale.B: The README's own description
rationale.C: That is Agent Studio / Agent Designer

stem: To let an ADK agent call the Gemini API through Vertex AI rather than the public API key path, which configuration is used?

options.B: Agent Gateway

rationale.A: The env-var pattern shown in the Memory Bank quickstart
rationale.B: Policy, not model routing

stem: What is the purpose of the 'Add current session' action in the ADK web UI's Eval tab?

options.A: Deploy the session to Cloud Run
options.B: Save the conversation as a new evaluation case in an evalset

rationale.B: Evalsets can be authored from real sessions in the UI

stem: A team asks whether to write an agent with ADK or with raw model SDK calls plus hand-written loops. Which reason favours ADK on the exam?

options.B: ADK provides agents, tools, workflow agents, sessions, evaluation and deploy commands in one framework
options.C: Raw SDK calls cannot call tools
options.D: ADK is required by Agent Gateway

rationale.B: The exam's 'open-source libraries (e.g., ADK)' bullet

stem: Which sequence of Memory Bank operations is correct?

options.B: CreateSession → AppendEvent (and ListEvents) → GenerateMemories → fetch memories in later sessions

rationale.B: The documented process

stem: Memories generated from a session are keyed to what scope by default?

options.B: The user id supplied on the session

rationale.B: All sessions carry a user id; memories map to that user

stem: A product wants an ADK agent to remember facts across conversations but only for the same end user, with no leakage between users. Which design?

options.A: One shared Memory Bank scope for all users
options.B: Memory Bank with memories scoped per user id and sessions carrying that id
options.C: Store facts in the system prompt

rationale.B: Per-user scoping is the documented model

stem: What is the difference between Agent Platform Sessions and Memory Bank?

options.B: Sessions store a conversation's chronological events; Memory Bank stores distilled long-term memories derived from them
options.C: Sessions are for Cloud Run only

rationale.B: The exam's core distinction
rationale.C: Both work with Runtime and other hosts
rationale.D: It stores generated memories, not transcripts

stem: After running the Agents CLI setup, where do its specialised skills get installed, and who can see them?

options.B: ~/.agents/skills, visible to Antigravity (global Antigravity CLI scope needs a move to ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/skills)

rationale.B: The tutorial's documented paths; verify against official docs
rationale.C: Registry holds agents/tools, not local skills

stem: The guide mentions 'agent vs. human mode' for Agents CLI skills. In an exam scenario, which requirement points to human mode?

options.A: Fully autonomous nightly batch of agent deployments
options.B: Each deploy or evaluation step must be reviewed and confirmed by an engineer before proceeding

rationale.B: Human mode = human in the loop on each step (semantics ⚠, direction from the guide)

stem: Which product is described as 'formerly Vector Search 2.0'?

options.B: Agent Retrieval

rationale.B: The Agent Retrieval overview says so

stem: A team already computes embeddings with their own model and wants to store them with metadata and filter by both similarity and payload fields. Which capability of Agent Retrieval fits?

options.B: Bring-your-own embeddings (BYOE) in collections with payload filtering

rationale.B: BYOE + unified vector/payload storage are documented features

stem: A small pilot with unpredictable traffic wants the cheapest way to start with Agent Retrieval. Which pricing model?

options.B: Usage-based

rationale.B: Docs: usage-based for smaller workloads

stem: A RAG system finds the right documents for most questions but misses some because the queries use synonyms not present in the text. What helps most?

options.B: A better embedding model or hybrid (lexical + vector) retrieval

rationale.A: Rerankers reorder what was retrieved; the problem is recall
rationale.B: Recall problems are fixed at the retrieval stage

stem: Which Agent Retrieval concept is analogous to a table in a relational database?

options.B: Collection

rationale.B: The overview's own analogy

stem: A company wants a fully managed RAG pipeline over enterprise datasets rather than assembling embeddings, storage and retrieval themselves. Which in-scope product?

options.B: Vector Search 1.0

rationale.A: Named as managed RAG for enterprise datasets
rationale.B: A vector index, not a pipeline

stem: Which authentication properties does Agent Identity provide by default?

options.B: Context-Aware Access with mTLS and DPoP-bound, unreplayable tokens

rationale.B: Documented credential security

stem: What form does an agent's identity string take in Agent Identity?

options.B: A SPIFFE ID mapped to the resource URI where the agent is hosted
options.C: A UUID chosen by the developer

rationale.B: Documented: SPIFFE-standard identity tied to the agent's lifecycle and resource

stem: In what protocol shape does a coding or ADK agent discover which tools an MCP server offers and invoke one?

options.B: JSON-RPC methods tools/list and tools/call

rationale.B: The MCP method names

stem: Which Agent Registry statement is correct for agents hosted on supported Google Cloud runtimes?

options.A: Registration always requires manual API calls
options.B: Registration happens automatically or via an opt-in step at deployment, depending on the runtime
options.C: Only Gemini Enterprise agents can be registered

rationale.B: The registry docs' summary

stem: A platform team must expose managed databases and third-party SaaS APIs to many agents through a consistent interface, with organisation-wide governance. Which combination?

options.A: Each agent embeds its own SDK calls
options.B: MCP servers (Google Cloud MCP Servers plus custom ones) registered in Agent Registry

rationale.B: The 3.2 bullet: registry + MCP servers for prebuilt and custom capabilities

stem: How does Agent Identity improve auditing when an agent acts on behalf of a user?

options.A: Logs show only the service account
options.B: Audit logs show both the agent's identity and the user's identity

rationale.B: Documented observability benefit

stem: What does an A2A agent card provide?

options.B: The agent's declared identity and capabilities (skills) so other agents can discover and delegate to it

rationale.B: A2A lets agents declare capabilities and identity; Registry extracts A2A skills

stem: A retrieval step must run, then a drafting step that depends on it, then a compliance check that depends on the draft. Which workflow type?

options.B: SequentialAgent

rationale.B: Dependent steps run in order

stem: An agent must retry a tool-using sub-workflow until a validator passes, with a maximum number of attempts. Which ADK construct is the natural fit?

options.B: LoopAgent with a termination condition and max iterations

rationale.B: Loops with a cap are the guard against reasoning loops (class name ⚠)

stem: Which mode of Agent Gateway applies when a Gemini Enterprise-hosted agent calls external tools?

options.B: Agent-to-Anywhere (egress)
options.D: Neither; Gemini Enterprise bypasses the gateway

rationale.B: Documented: Gemini Enterprise supports only egress mode
rationale.C: Runtime supports both; Gemini Enterprise only egress
rationale.D: Managed runtimes route through the gateway automatically

stem: Which set of products does the guide name for coordinating multi-agent handoffs and workflows?

options.B: Agent Identity, Agent Registry, Agent Runtime, agent policies

rationale.B: The 3.3 bullet verbatim

stem: Two agents inside one ADK application need to hand off control based on the LLM's judgement rather than a fixed order. Which mechanism?

options.B: LLM-driven transfer to a sub-agent within the same ADK agent tree

rationale.B: ADK supports delegation to sub-agents (exact API ⚠)

stem: What does ADK's tool-trajectory evaluation compare?

options.B: The sequence of tool calls the agent made against the expected sequence

rationale.B: Trajectory = tool call sequence

stem: Which ADK evaluation criteria require a Google Cloud project to run?

options.B: safety_v1 and the multi-turn trajectory-quality criterion, which delegate to the Agent Platform Eval SDK
options.C: None; ADK eval is fully local

rationale.B: Documented: these delegate to the Agent Platform Eval SDK and need GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT/LOCATION

stem: A team wants to guard against regressions by comparing live agent behaviour to previously recorded, verified interactions. Which ADK command?

options.B: adk conformance test

rationale.B: Conformance testing against a golden baseline

stem: Your evalset has expected responses that are paraphrases of what the agent says. Exact match fails. What is the ADK-native adjustment?

options.B: Use response_match_score with a threshold (default 0.8) that tolerates wording differences

rationale.B: Documented default allows a margin of error
rationale.D: Does not address paraphrase in references

stem: Which is the correct order to build a continuous evaluation pipeline for tool execution?

options.A: Deploy, then write tests after incidents
options.B: Define success criteria → build evalset with golden data and edge cases → run in CI on every change and on production samples

rationale.B: The 4.1 bullets in order

stem: Product wants to measure whether answers are grounded in retrieved context, at scale, with model-based judges provided by the platform. Which choice?

options.B: Agent Platform Gen AI evaluation service

rationale.B: Managed evaluation on the Optimize pillar

stem: When would a custom autorater be preferred over the managed evaluation service?

options.B: When the success criterion is domain-specific and not covered by built-in metrics
options.D: When the agent runs on Cloud Run

rationale.B: Bespoke rubric = custom judge

stem: Where can an ADK evalset be created without writing JSON by hand?

options.B: The Eval tab in adk web, from a real session

rationale.B: Documented UI flow

stem: Which ADK deploy target lands the agent on the managed runtime formerly called Agent Engine?

options.B: adk deploy agent_engine

rationale.B: Agent Runtime kept the agent_engine name in tooling

stem: An agent on Cloud Run must keep per-user conversation state across requests. What is the exam-preferred managed approach?

options.B: Agent Platform Sessions (via an Agent Runtime instance as session store) and optionally Memory Bank
options.C: Sticky sessions on the load balancer

rationale.B: Documented Cloud Run + Sessions/Memory Bank notebook pattern

stem: What does Agent Runtime add beyond hosting?

options.B: Sessions, Memory Bank, code execution sandbox, Example Store (preview), automatic Registry and Gateway integration, observability

rationale.B: Runtime overview + Gateway/Registry docs

stem: A bursty internal tool has minutes of idle time between requests and a strict 'pay nothing when idle' requirement, with a custom container. Which runtime?

options.B: Cloud Run (scale to zero)

rationale.B: Serverless containers scale to zero
rationale.D: Custom container requirement points to Cloud Run

stem: Which factor does the guide say should drive runtime selection?

options.B: Use case, requirements and cost

rationale.B: The 4.2 bullet

stem: An agent on Agent Runtime needs Model Armor screening via Agent Gateway in Client-to-Agent mode. Which IAM roles must the Reasoning Engine service agent hold?

options.B: roles/modelarmor.calloutUser in the agent project and roles/modelarmor.user in the template project

rationale.B: Documented role pair

stem: Where do you look first for Runtime agent errors in Cloud Logging?

options.B: resource.type=aiplatform.googleapis.com/ReasoningEngine with the location label

rationale.B: Documented filter

stem: An agent's answers are fine in tests but production users report growing inaccuracy over weeks with no code change. What is this and how do you detect it?

options.B: Drift; continuous evaluation of production samples against the golden set

rationale.B: Drift is gradual quality change; detection is continuous evaluation

stem: Which is the most direct cost optimisation for an agent whose traces show long prompts full of stale tool results?

options.B: Trim or summarise context between steps and cache stable tool results

rationale.B: Attacks the cause seen in traces
rationale.D: Hosting does not fix prompt bloat

stem: A tool call fails intermittently with timeouts and the agent then hallucinates a result. What is the right fix set?

options.B: Return explicit tool errors to the model, add retries with backoff and instruct the agent to report failure; monitor with Cloud Trace/Logging

rationale.B: Handles the failure honestly and observably

stem: Which pair makes up Google Cloud Observability as listed in the exam guide?

options.B: Cloud Logging and Cloud Trace

rationale.B: The guide's parenthetical

stem: On the Agent Platform Optimize pillar, which view helps understand how agents, tools and services are connected?

options.B: Billing

rationale.A: Named alongside Cloud Observability in the agents overview
rationale.B: No

stem: What does Agent Gateway use by default to authenticate agents, endpoints and servers?

options.B: Identity-Aware Proxy using IAM policies

rationale.B: Documented default

stem: Which statement about Agent Registry entries and Agent Gateway is correct?

options.B: Agents and any endpoints, servers or tools they connect to must all be registered with Agent Registry

rationale.B: Documented requirement

stem: Beyond IAM, what additional control type can Agent Gateway apply to protect against toxic combinations of tools?

options.B: Natural-language, context-aware controls on agents

rationale.B: Documented optional control

stem: Model Armor can be configured at which two levels for Agent Platform traffic?

options.B: Floor settings (project-level) and templates (per request)

rationale.B: Documented

stem: What happens to a request if Model Armor is unavailable in the region or temporarily unreachable when integrated with Agent Platform?

options.B: The request continues without sanitisation (fail open)

rationale.B: Documented: processing continues, exposing unscreened traffic

stem: Which content does Model Armor NOT screen in the Agent Gateway and Agent Platform integrations?

options.B: Documents (document screening is only supported in the Gemini Enterprise integration)

rationale.B: Documented limitation

stem: What is the Model Armor input size limit and its behaviour above it?

options.B: 4 MB, content above the limit is skipped

rationale.B: Documented

stem: An agent must call a partner API on behalf of users using OAuth 2.0. Which component manages the flow and credential handling on Agent Platform?

options.B: The auth manager associated with Agent Identity

rationale.B: Documented: automates OAuth flows and manages keys

stem: Which combination best implements 'defence in depth' for an agent that can act on external systems?

options.B: Agent Identity + PAB, Agent Gateway authorization policy, Model Armor screening, HITL for consequential actions, audit logs with agent and user identity

rationale.B: The full Section 5 stack

stem: Which Model Armor mode should you choose while validating a template so violations are logged but not blocked?

options.B: Inspect-only (log violations)

rationale.B: Documented: inspect and log only

stem: Which concepts does Antigravity CLI carry over from Gemini CLI, per Google's transition announcement?

options.B: Agent Skills, Hooks, Subagents and Extensions

rationale.B: The announcement's list

stem: What is the documented directory layout of an Antigravity skill?

options.B: A folder with SKILL.md plus optional scripts/, references/ and assets/

rationale.B: The codelab's structure

stem: How does Antigravity decide to use a skill?

options.A: The user must type its name
options.B: It selects based on the skill's description matching the task context; it can also be referenced directly

rationale.B: Documented behaviour; write descriptions with task keywords

stem: Which Antigravity setting controls whether terminal commands run automatically?

options.B: Terminal Command Auto Execution: Request Review vs Always Proceed

rationale.B: Documented autonomy control

stem: A coding agent must run on a shared team environment with controlled tooling and no local installs, inside Google Cloud. Which is the sandbox product named by the guide?

options.B: Cloud Shell only

rationale.A: Named in 2.1 alongside GKE and Antigravity
rationale.B: Not listed

stem: Why does the guide list 'optimise execution runtimes' as a coding-agent task, and what must accompany it?

options.B: Agents can profile and rewrite hot paths, but changes need benchmarks and tests as evidence

rationale.B: Verify-then-claim

stem: Which Antigravity file is read as a standing rule set for the whole project?

options.B: AGENTS.md (and GEMINI.md)

rationale.B: Documented

stem: A team wants a security reviewer, a test writer and a doc updater as separately invokable specialists inside Antigravity. Which customisation type?

options.B: Subagents (custom agents defined by agent.md personas)

rationale.B: Subagents are delegated specialists

stem: Which is the correct pairing of a customisation with its role?

options.A: Hook = packaged knowledge; Skill = lifecycle interception
options.B: Skill = packaged know-how; Rule = standing instruction; Hook = lifecycle interception; Plugin/extension = bundle; Subagent = delegated worker

rationale.B: The vocabulary the 2.2 bullet lists

stem: A global rule should force a 'safe migration' skill whenever a database schema changes. Is this composable in Antigravity?

options.A: No, rules and skills cannot interact
options.B: Yes; the codelab gives exactly this example of a rule enforcing a skill

rationale.B: Documented example

stem: Which low-code product is described in Agent Platform docs as a visual canvas for designing agent reasoning loops and workflows?

options.B: Agent Registry

rationale.A: Named in the overview (exam wording: Agent Designer / CX Agent Studio)
rationale.B: Catalog

stem: A flow must ask for a date until a valid one is given, then move on. Which constructs?

options.A: A page with a required parameter, a transition route on parameter fill, and a no-input/no-match event handler that re-prompts
options.B: A webhook that ends the session

rationale.B: Destructive

stem: Where does a chain-of-thought prompt template belong in the low-code world?

options.B: In the in-console system instructions / prompt template of Agent Designer or CX Agent Studio

rationale.B: The 1.1 bullet

stem: When is Agent Designer (instruction-driven) preferable to a CX Agent Studio state machine?

options.A: When every step must be deterministic
options.B: When the task is open-ended assistance guided by instructions and connected data rather than fixed pages

rationale.B: Instruction agents suit open-ended tasks

stem: What does Agent Search bring to a Gemini Enterprise agent?

options.B: Semantic search over connected enterprise data with access control

rationale.B: Ex Vertex AI Search: search engines tailored to your data

stem: Which is a risk if enterprise data is connected to an agent without honouring source permissions?

options.B: Users see documents they are not authorised to see

rationale.B: The securely-connect requirement in 1.2

stem: The company's knowledge lives in recorded meetings and product images. Which 1.2 capability is being tested?

options.B: Ingesting and processing unstructured multimodal data into the workflow

rationale.B: The multimodal ingestion bullet

stem: A Gemini Enterprise agent must answer from a SharePoint-like repository and a ticketing SaaS. What is the low-code way?

options.B: Configure Gemini Enterprise data connectors to those sources

rationale.B: Connectors are the low-code data path
